interest: Reveals private consultant involvement in U.S. consular intelligence on Japan's subsidized synthetic fiber and media leaks.
overview: This file documents U.S. State Department inquiries and consular reporting on the rapid development of Japan's staple fiber (artificial wool) and rayon industries between 1934 and 1936. Prompted by inquiries from American textile consultant Joseph D. Holmes, the American Consulate General in Tokyo compiled comprehensive investigative reports on Japanese production capacity, manufacturing facilities, government subsidies, military uses, and commercial applications, alongside the collection and distribution of fiber samples. The records also chronicle industry interest and trade press coverage after a confidential consular report was leaked to the Daily News Record, as well as negotiations regarding the sale of Sanforizing patent rights to Japan.
